sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Over the summer, a new movement started to gain momentum.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，一场新的运动开始蓄势待发。

sentences.en: The movement to ban plastic drinking straws.
sentences.zh: 一场禁止使用塑料吸管的运动。

sentences.en: It's now legal for food service businesses in Seattle to provide plastic straws and utensils.
sentences.zh: 目前，西雅图的餐饮企业提供塑料吸管和餐具是合法的。

sentences.en: Santa Cruz is among 28 others around the country that have banned or limited plastic straws or are considering it.
sentences.zh: 圣克鲁斯是全国其他28个已经禁止或限制塑料吸管，或者正在考虑此举的城市之一。

sentences.en: California and Hawaii are even exploring statewide policies.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州和夏威夷州甚至正在探索全州范围内的政策。

sentences.en: Environmentalists say 500 million plastic straws end up in the world's oceans every year, harming wildlife.
sentences.zh: 环保人士称，每年有5亿根塑料吸管最终流入世界海洋，危害野生动物。

sentences.en: The argument against straws is pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 反对吸管的理由非常简单。

sentences.en: We consume tons of plastic.
sentences.zh: 我们消耗了大量的塑料。

sentences.en: Not much of it gets recycled.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分并没有被回收。

sentences.en: Most of it ends up in landfills and oceans.
sentences.zh: 大部分最终进入了垃圾填埋场和海洋。

sentences.en: So why not try to reduce a little of that waste?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么不试着减少一点这种浪费呢？

sentences.en: But like most issues these days, there's been a lot of disagreement about it.
sentences.zh: 但就像如今大多数问题一样，关于这一点一直存在很多分歧。

sentences.en: There's been backlash from a few directions, including conservatives.
sentences.zh: 来自包括保守派在内的多个方向都有抵制的声音。

sentences.en: The left's war against, wait for it, straws.
sentences.zh: 左派发起的针对——等等，听好了——吸管的战争。

sentences.en: It's all a bunch of moral preening, right?
sentences.zh: 这全是一堆道德作秀，对吧？

sentences.en: It's this idea that we are holier than thou.
sentences.zh: 这是一种我们比你们更高尚的想法。

sentences.en: But people with disabilities also spoke up because some of those folks actually need straws in order to drink.
sentences.zh: 但残疾人士也发声了，因为他们中的一些人确实需要吸管才能喝水。

sentences.en: That it might take away their tool of independence.
sentences.zh: 这可能会剥夺他们独立的工具。

sentences.en: And there's even disagreement about the actual number of straws that we throw away each day.
sentences.zh: 甚至对于我们每天扔掉的吸管的实际数量也存在分歧。

sentences.en: You hear the number 500 million floating around a lot.
sentences.zh: 你经常听到5亿这个数字。

sentences.en: Apparently, that number came not from a rigorous study, but from a precocious nine-year-old's science project.
sentences.zh: 显然，这个数字并非来自严谨的研究，而是来自一个早熟的九岁孩子的科学项目。

sentences.en: Not a nine-year-old's science project.
sentences.zh: 不是九岁孩子的科学项目。

sentences.en: A nine-year-old's science project.
sentences.zh: 是一个九岁孩子的科学项目。

sentences.en: But this has really taken off, right?
sentences.zh: 但这确实火起来了，对吧？

sentences.en: Even the environmentalists could not agree on whether the straw ban was a good thing or not.
sentences.zh: 即使是环保人士也无法就禁塑吸管是否是一件好事达成一致。

sentences.en: Yeah, everybody got to have their thing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，每个人都得有自己的主张。

sentences.en: The real problem is cars.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是汽车。

sentences.en: The real problem is buildings.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是建筑。

sentences.en: The real problem is, have you seen China's emissions?
sentences.zh: 真正的问题是，你看到中国的排放量了吗？

sentences.en: You know, the real problem is too much nitrogen and, you know, ocean acidification and, you know, just any environmental problem is probably more important than plastic straws.
sentences.zh: 你知道，真正的问题是过多的氮，还有，你知道，海洋酸化，而且，你知道，任何环境问题可能都比塑料吸管更重要。

sentences.en: This is journalist Alexis Madrigal.
sentences.zh: 这位是记者亚历克西斯·马德里加尔。
zh_words: 亚历克西斯·马德里加尔

sentences.en: He wrote a great essay about plastic straws for The Atlantic, and he's going to be our guide through all of this.
sentences.zh: 他为《大西洋月刊》写了一篇关于塑料吸管的精彩文章，他将成为我们了解这一切的向导。

sentences.en: Because he says that when you zoom out from the controversies of today and look at the actual history of plastic straws, they can tell us a lot about America.
sentences.zh: 因为他说，当你从今天的争议中抽离出来，审视塑料吸管的真实历史时，它们能告诉我们很多关于美国的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So tell me about some of those bigger themes that emerged when you looked at the history of plastic straws.
sentences.zh: 那么，请告诉我当你审视塑料吸管的历史时，出现的一些更大的主题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, I used to do this quite a bit, like just take some little object and just trace its history.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我过去经常做这种事，就是拿一些小物件，然后追溯它的历史。

sentences.en: You know, you can look up the patents on Google and you can search around for, you know, the companies that made it and you can see its technical evolution.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以在谷歌上查找专利，可以搜索制造它的公司，可以看到它的技术演变。

sentences.en: You know, you can just look at it like the way you would look at the development of any technology.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以像看待任何技术的发展一样看待它。

sentences.en: But the thing that was so crazy about the straw was that it just hit so many of these like real true major trends in the way that the country worked.
sentences.zh: 但关于吸管最疯狂的事情是，它触及了这么多国家运作方式中真正重大的趋势。

sentences.en: You know, the straw is there for the invention of American industrialism, for urbanization, for public health reform, for like the suburbanization of the country, fast food.
sentences.zh: 你知道，吸管见证了美国工业主义的发明、城市化、公共卫生改革，以及国家的郊区化、快餐业。

sentences.en: And now, of course, the culture wars, like it's there for all of that.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在还有文化战争，它也见证了这一切。

sentences.en: And so tell me where it all began.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我这一切是从哪里开始的。

sentences.en: Did someone invent the straw or was it just always there?
sentences.zh: 是有人发明了吸管，还是它一直都在那里？

sentences.en: So, you know, there's even like scientific studies that show that orangutans like will go like, hey, this straw like thing is cool for doing straw like stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，甚至有科学研究表明，红毛猩猩会说，嘿，这种像吸管的东西对于做吸管类的事情很酷。

sentences.en: So, you know, so it's probably been around forever.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它可能一直存在。

sentences.en: There's ancient versions, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 有古代版本，等等。

sentences.en: But in 19th century America, basically the straw was rye, literally, you know, grass that grows and it's kind of got this hollow tube.
sentences.zh: 但在19世纪的美国，基本上吸管是黑麦，字面意思，你知道，生长出来的草，它有一种中空的管子。

sentences.en: And, you know, you dry it, you cut it into shape and that's what would happen.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你把它弄干，剪成形状，这就是会发生的事情。

sentences.en: That was the straw.
sentences.zh: 那就是吸管。

sentences.en: Straw was straw.
sentences.zh: 吸管就是吸管。

sentences.en: Around this time, there were also straws made out of more durable materials like metal and glass.
sentences.zh: 大约在这个时候，还有用金属和玻璃等更耐用材料制成的吸管。

sentences.en: But then.
sentences.zh: 但是后来。

sentences.en: Then, you know, along comes this guy in 1888 named Marvin Stone, and he creates what was then called the artificial straw.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，1888年出现了一个叫马文·斯通的人，他创造了当时所谓的“人造吸管”。

sentences.en: And the artificial straw is basically paper dipped in some kind of waxy substance like paraffin.
sentences.zh: 人造吸管基本上就是浸泡在某种蜡质物质（如石蜡）中的纸。

sentences.en: And that becomes this new standard.
sentences.zh: 这就成了新的标准。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just that it was artificial.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为它是人造的。

sentences.en: It's also that it was disposable, this straw.
sentences.zh: 也是因为它是可丢弃的，这种吸管。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This was basically this incredibly cheap and this incredibly basically disposable and hygienic thing.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种极其便宜、极其可丢弃且卫生的东西。

sentences.en: This wasn't something that came from nature.
sentences.zh: 这不是来自自然的东西。

sentences.en: It was, in fact, produced to a standard.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它是按标准生产的。

sentences.en: You know, this was a patent straw.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种专利吸管。

sentences.en: And the fact that this straw was hygienic and produced to a standard was important because straws were becoming a tool in the emerging public health movement that was happening in cities around this time.
sentences.zh: 这种吸管卫生且按标准生产的事实很重要，因为吸管正成为当时城市中新兴公共卫生运动的一种工具。

sentences.en: So, you know, the reason public health is emerging at this time is because people in American cities are just like dying all the time of communicable diseases.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，公共卫生在此时兴起的原因是美国城市里的人们一直在死于传染病。

sentences.en: And a lot of illnesses were spread through dirty drinking water.
sentences.zh: 而且很多疾病是通过肮脏的饮用水传播的。

sentences.en: To understand why this was such a big health issue and why straws would eventually help to solve it, you have to understand how public water fountains worked at the time.
sentences.zh: 要理解为什么这是一个如此大的健康问题，以及为什么吸管最终会帮助解决它，你必须了解当时的公共饮水机是如何工作的。

sentences.en: In a lot of places in the city, both workplaces and in public locations, the water fountain wasn't like what we think of now,
sentences.zh: 在城市里的很多地方，包括工作场所和公共场所，饮水机不像我们现在想的那样，

sentences.en: like this little thing with water bubbling out of it or like you press a little button, water comes out.
sentences.zh: 像这种水冒出来的小东西，或者你按一个小按钮，水就出来了。

sentences.en: It was just kind of like water that was sitting there or a little tap.
sentences.zh: 它只是像放在那里的水，或者一个小水龙头。

sentences.en: And you would actually fill a cup that was attached to it and just drink out of it.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会装满一个附在上面的杯子，然后直接喝。

sentences.en: And it'd be like, you know, on some kind of chain or whatever.
sentences.zh: 它会像，你知道，挂在某种链子上之类的。

sentences.en: So, you know, a bunch of different people would all drink from the same cup.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，很多人都会从同一个杯子里喝水。

sentences.en: We actually did an episode about this.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上做过一期关于这个的节目。

sentences.en: These early water fountains use something called the common cup.
sentences.zh: 这些早期的饮水机使用一种叫做“公共杯”的东西。

sentences.en: And it became one of the main targets of the public health campaigners.
sentences.zh: 它成为了公共卫生运动者的主要目标之一。

sentences.en: There was actually like one Kansas doctor who started to like push this campaign against the common cup.
sentences.zh: 实际上有一位堪萨斯州的医生开始推动这场反对公共杯的运动。

sentences.en: And the tone of this campaign, it's intense.
sentences.zh: 这场运动的基调非常强烈。

sentences.en: They literally would show the grim reaper taking a drink from the common cup with like a little girl next to him.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至会展示死神拿着公共杯喝水，旁边还有一个小女孩。

sentences.en: And you'd just be like, Jesus, man, they're just drinking from the same cup, you know.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，天哪，伙计，他们只是在喝同一个杯子里的水，你知道。

sentences.en: And in times when you want public health reform or some kind of reform, you just need to go for the throat.
sentences.zh: 在你想进行公共卫生改革或某种改革的时候，你只需要直击要害。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like this is going to kill your children.
sentences.zh: 就像这会杀死你的孩子。

sentences.en: You know, that's like that's where they went with it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是他们采取的方式。

sentences.en: A lot of cities began requiring straw dispensers in certain public spaces.
sentences.zh: 许多城市开始要求在某些公共场所安装吸管分配器。

sentences.en: In the case of the common cup, straws were a way to avoid actually putting your mouth where somebody else's mouth had been.
sentences.zh: 在公共杯的情况下，吸管是一种避免把嘴放在别人嘴放过的地方的方法。

sentences.en: But it wasn't just public health reformers that contributed to the rise of straws.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是公共卫生改革者促成了吸管的兴起。

sentences.en: There's two things.
sentences.zh: 有两件事。

sentences.en: There's a sort of public health mania on the one side.
sentences.zh: 一方面是一种公共卫生狂热。

sentences.en: And on the other side, there's the development of a certain bubbly carbonated beverage called soda.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，是一种叫做“苏打水”的起泡碳酸饮料的发展。

sentences.en: And the soda fountain occupies this really important place in the kind of late 19th century, early 20th century city just as a space.
sentences.zh: 苏打水喷泉在19世纪末、20世纪初的城市中占据了一个非常重要的空间位置。

sentences.en: For one, most of the public places where you could go have a drink were saloons.
sentences.zh: 首先，大多数你可以去喝一杯的公共场所都是酒吧。

sentences.en: And saloons were primarily gendered male.
sentences.zh: 而酒吧主要是男性化的。

sentences.en: Urban women with increasing freedoms in the city wanted a place to go.
sentences.zh: 在城市中拥有越来越多自由的城市女性想要一个去处。

sentences.en: And many urban women were also involved in various temperance movements.
sentences.zh: 许多城市女性也参与了各种禁酒运动。

sentences.en: And again, saloons, they're serving booze there.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，酒吧，他们在那里供应酒。

sentences.en: And soda fountains become this kind of like clean, healthy alternative.
sentences.zh: 而苏打水喷泉成为了一种干净、健康的替代品。

sentences.en: So there are all these various trends, urbanization, the rise of the soda fountain, the temperance movement, the rise of public health.
sentences.zh: 所以有所有这些不同的趋势，城市化、苏打水喷泉的兴起、禁酒运动、公共卫生的兴起。

sentences.en: They all help lead to this booming, strong industry, really.
sentences.zh: 它们都帮助引领了一个蓬勃发展的强大产业，真的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's amazing because if you look at there's the Battle Creek Inquirer, you know, small paper in May of 1924,
sentences.zh: 而且令人惊奇的是，如果你看看《巴特尔克里克问询报》，你知道，1924年5月的一份小报纸，

sentences.en: they actually sort of list out how far did this go?
sentences.zh: 他们实际上列出了这发展到了什么程度？

sentences.en: You know, how big was this boom?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种繁荣有多大？

sentences.en: And they say, due to the Yankee mania for sanitation, the output of artificial straws has increased from 165 million in 1901 to 4 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 他们说，由于美国人对卫生的狂热，人造吸管的产量从1901年的1.65亿根增加到每年40亿根。

sentences.en: A manufacturer pointed out yesterday that laid end to end, these straws would build an ants subway 16 times around the world at the equator.
sentences.zh: 一位制造商昨天指出，如果把这些吸管首尾相连，它们可以绕赤道建造一条蚂蚁地铁16次。

sentences.en: And so 4 billion straws.
sentences.zh: 所以40亿根吸管。

sentences.en: In context, you're talking about America has 114 million people at that point.
sentences.zh: 在当时，美国有1.14亿人口。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So 35 straws per capita.
sentences.zh: 所以人均35根吸管。

sentences.en: That's a lot of straws.
sentences.zh: 那可是很多吸管。

sentences.en: That's a lot of straws.
sentences.zh: 那可是很多吸管。

sentences.en: And more of this tiny, kind of insignificant object surfing along much bigger trends.
sentences.zh: 还有更多这种微小的、微不足道的物体在更大的趋势中随波逐流。

sentences.en: Trends like the rise of fast food culture.
sentences.zh: 像快餐文化兴起这样的趋势。

sentences.en: Introducing the world's newest, silliest, and hamburger-eatingest clown, Ronald McDonald.
sentences.zh: 向世界介绍最新、最傻、最爱吃汉堡的小丑，罗纳德·麦当劳。

sentences.en: Before a businessman named Ray Kroc took over a little restaurant in Southern California called McDonald's, he was a paper cup salesman.
sentences.zh: 在一位名叫雷·克洛克的商人接管南加州一家名为麦当劳的小餐馆之前，他是一名纸杯推销员。

sentences.en: Which meant that he was also a straw salesman.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他也是一名吸管推销员。

sentences.en: So he worked for the Lily Tulip Paper Company for a long time, like 15 years, going around the Midwest, selling straws and cups to soda fountains.
sentences.zh: 所以他在莉莉郁金香纸业公司工作了很长时间，大约15年，在中西部到处跑，向苏打水喷泉推销吸管和杯子。

sentences.en: But what's amazing to hear, you know, and he wrote a memoir, which, I mean, he ran a burger shop and he called his memoir Grinding It Out.
sentences.zh: 但听到这些令人惊奇，你知道，他写了一本回忆录，我的意思是，他经营一家汉堡店，他把他的回忆录命名为《磨砺》。

sentences.en: Which I think kind of tells you a little bit about him.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这多少能让你了解他一点。

sentences.en: He also turns out he like moonlighted as a pianist when he was a salesman.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他做推销员时还兼职做钢琴家。

sentences.en: And, like, just kind of one of those, like, really doesn't feel like a 21st century story.
sentences.zh: 而且，就像，真的感觉不像是一个21世纪的故事。

sentences.en: Like, it feels like a, like a, wow, that's a weird story.
sentences.zh: 就像，感觉像是一个，哇，那是一个奇怪的故事。

sentences.en: But Ray Kroc, in this memoir, Grinding It Out, he describes paper cups in this kind of disposable, you know, hygienic world.
sentences.zh: 但雷·克洛克在这本回忆录《磨砺》中，描述了这种可丢弃的、你知道，卫生的世界里的纸杯。

sentences.en: He was like, they were innovative and upbeat.
sentences.zh: 他说，它们是创新的、乐观的。

sentences.en: He said, I sensed from the outset that paper cups were part of the way America was headed.
sentences.zh: 他说，我从一开始就感觉到纸杯是美国发展方向的一部分。

sentences.en: He was right.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。

sentences.en: Like, that was part of the way America was going.
sentences.zh: 就像，那是美国发展方向的一部分。

sentences.en: Like, every, we were going to throw away everything.
sentences.zh: 就像，每一样，我们要扔掉所有东西。

sentences.en: We throw away f***ing phones, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 我们扔掉该死的手机，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, we throw away computers.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们扔掉电脑。

sentences.en: We throw away couches, you know?
sentences.zh: 我们扔掉沙发，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So Kroc becomes a central figure, at least in my story, because he sort of connects this paper cup industry to this greater concept of, like, disposability in America.
sentences.zh: 所以克洛克成为了一个核心人物，至少在我的故事里，因为他把这种纸杯工业与美国这种更大的“可丢弃性”概念联系了起来。

sentences.en: Selling all those cups brought Ray Kroc into contact with soda fountains.
sentences.zh: 销售所有这些杯子让雷·克洛克接触到了苏打水喷泉。

sentences.en: And he eventually went into business selling milkshake mixers.
sentences.zh: 他最终开始从事销售奶昔搅拌机的生意。

sentences.en: This led him to Southern California, where he saw the first McDonald's in operation.
sentences.zh: 这把他带到了南加州，在那里他看到了第一家麦当劳的运营。

sentences.en: He bought his way into the small company and ousted the original owners.
sentences.zh: 他买下了这家小公司，并赶走了原来的所有者。

sentences.en: In the 60s, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 在60年代，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: McDonald's goes from basically like 100 franchises to 1,000.
sentences.zh: 麦当劳从基本上100家特许经营店发展到1000家。

sentences.en: And then just, like, keeps on going.
sentences.zh: 然后就一直，像这样，继续下去。

sentences.en: Pure, like, kind of hockey stick growth.
sentences.zh: 纯粹的，像那种曲棍球杆式的增长。

sentences.en: The American public are basically beef-eating people.
sentences.zh: 美国公众基本上是吃牛肉的人。

sentences.en: And it wears well, day after day after day after day.
sentences.zh: 而且它很受欢迎，日复一日，日复一日。

sentences.en: People just want more of it.
sentences.zh: 人们只是想要更多。

sentences.en: And I can't give them everything they like, but this one thing I sure can give.
sentences.zh: 我不能给他们所有他们喜欢的，但这一个我肯定能给。

sentences.en: And you have, with basically the rise of fast food and suburbia, this massive increase in the amount of just kind of wrapping, basically, for food.
sentences.zh: 而且，随着快餐和郊区的兴起，你基本上有了食物包装数量的巨大增加。

sentences.en: You're getting your food in a box.
sentences.zh: 你把食物装在盒子里。

sentences.en: And that just hadn't been the way that things were traditionally done.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是传统做事的方式。

sentences.en: So, like, the plastic industry, at the same time, is growing up because of this disposable trend.
sentences.zh: 所以，塑料工业，在同一时间，因为这种可丢弃的趋势而成长起来。

sentences.en: Can you talk about this transition from paper straws to plastic straws?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈从纸吸管到塑料吸管的这种转变吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: One thing that's interesting about plastics, you know, 1950, the world is only producing, like, one and a half million tons of plastic.
sentences.zh: 关于塑料，有一点很有趣，你知道，1950年，全世界的塑料产量只有大约150万吨。

sentences.en: Which, of course, is a lot, because plastic doesn't weigh very much.
sentences.zh: 当然，这已经很多了，因为塑料本身并不重。

sentences.en: But it's not, it's nowhere close to sort of where we get.
sentences.zh: 但它还远没达到我们后来那种程度。

sentences.en: I mean, by the late 60s, that production has grown tenfold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，到了60年代末，产量已经增长了十倍。

sentences.en: So, it's really kind of in the 50s into the 60s, where basically people are going, is there an object?
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上是在50年代到60年代期间，人们基本上都在想，有没有什么东西？

sentences.en: Maybe it should be plastic, you know?
sentences.zh: 也许它应该是塑料做的，你懂的？

sentences.en: And so, you know, chairs become plastic and plates become plastic and just everything kind of, if you can do it, you can do it in plastic.
sentences.zh: 于是，椅子变成了塑料的，盘子变成了塑料的，只要能做成塑料的，就都用塑料做。

sentences.en: And so, of course, straws become part of this.
sentences.zh: 当然，吸管也成了其中的一部分。

sentences.en: By the 1970s and 80s, plastic straws had become ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 到了1970和80年代，塑料吸管已经无处不在了。

sentences.en: They were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们随处可见。

sentences.en: And while straw design continued to evolve slightly, the more dramatic changes were happening in the straw industry.
sentences.zh: 虽然吸管的设计仍在不断微调，但更剧烈的变化发生在吸管行业内部。

sentences.en: At this point, both in our economy and also in the sort of, like, the straws history,
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，无论是在我们的经济中，还是在吸管的历史中，

sentences.en: it's really the mechanisms that organize the factories that become the most interesting sort of object.
sentences.zh: 真正成为最有趣对象的，其实是组织工厂运作的机制。

sentences.en: And those mechanisms are basically financial capitalism beginning to really move away from being about family businesses, organizing production, you know,
sentences.zh: 这些机制基本上就是金融资本主义，开始真正脱离那种家族企业模式来组织生产，你知道，

sentences.en: at these kind of local levels or regional levels.
sentences.zh: 在这些地方层面或区域层面。

sentences.en: And it really becomes everything is just a money waiting to be made through financialization.
sentences.zh: 最终一切都变成了通过金融化来赚取利润。

sentences.en: By financialization, Lexus is talking about a big trend in economics that's been happening over the last few decades.
sentences.zh: Lexus所说的“金融化”是指过去几十年来经济领域的一个大趋势。

sentences.en: Our manufacturing sector has been shrinking, while our financial sector has been expanding,
sentences.zh: 我们的制造业在萎缩，而金融业在扩张，

sentences.en: which has big implications for who ends up making money on straws and a million other consumer goods.
sentences.zh: 这对谁最终能从吸管和数百万种其他消费品中获利有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: The slice of money that's going to the people who provide the money as opposed to provide the products is growing.
sentences.zh: 流向提供资金的人的钱，相对于流向提供产品的人的钱，所占比例正在增加。

sentences.en: And that has really important consequences for how things get made and who makes them and where the factories are located and how many people are employed and the culture of work and all these things.
sentences.zh: 这对产品的制造方式、制造者、工厂选址、雇佣人数、工作文化以及所有这些事情都产生了非常重要的后果。

sentences.en: So tell me what happened to Maryland Cup.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，Maryland Cup公司发生了什么？

sentences.en: This is one of the country's biggest straw makers.
sentences.zh: 这是该国最大的吸管制造商之一。

sentences.en: What happened to them around this time?
sentences.zh: 那段时间他们发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Maryland Cup is just a classic American story, right?
sentences.zh: Maryland Cup的故事是一个典型的美国故事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's owned by these brothers, the Shapiro brothers.
sentences.zh: 它由Shapiro兄弟拥有。

sentences.en: They started out as like a bakery and then they turn into this kind of bakery services provider and then they start making straws.
sentences.zh: 他们起初是做面包店的，后来变成了某种烘焙服务提供商，然后开始制造吸管。

sentences.en: So after they make straws, they make cups.
sentences.zh: 在制造吸管之后，他们开始制造杯子。

sentences.en: After they make cups, they get sort of become one of the big partners for McDonald's.
sentences.zh: 在制造杯子之后，他们成为了麦当劳的大合作伙伴之一。

sentences.en: And it remained basically family owned.
sentences.zh: 而且它基本上一直保持着家族所有制。

sentences.en: But eventually, you know, the original management is gone.
sentences.zh: 但最终，你知道，最初的管理层离开了。

sentences.en: The people are aging and they decide that they're going to sell the company.
sentences.zh: 人们老了，他们决定卖掉公司。

sentences.en: They sell the company to another company called Fort Howard.
sentences.zh: 他们把公司卖给了另一家叫Fort Howard的公司。

sentences.en: And they had one of these kind of hard charging CEOs.
sentences.zh: 他们有一位那种雷厉风行的首席执行官。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a great story in the Baltimore Sun where they describe going to the sales meeting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，《巴尔的摩太阳报》上有一个很棒的故事，描述了他们去参加销售会议的情景。

sentences.en: You know, the Maryland Cup executives like all show up and the new bosses are there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Maryland Cup的高管们都到了，新老板也在场。

sentences.en: And he literally apparently had a flip chart.
sentences.zh: 显然他真的带了一个翻页挂图。

sentences.en: And on the one page of the flip chart, it said, here are your old values.
sentences.zh: 在翻页挂图的第一页上，写着：这是你们的旧价值观。

sentences.en: And they were service, quality, responding to customers.
sentences.zh: 它们是服务、质量、响应客户。

sentences.en: And then apparently he literally like flipped the flip chart to the next page.
sentences.zh: 然后显然他真的翻到了下一页。

sentences.en: And it said, new values, profits, profits, profits.
sentences.zh: 上面写着：新价值观，利润，利润，利润。

sentences.en: I was like, damn, that's quite a PowerPoint, you know.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，这PPT真是绝了，你懂的。

sentences.en: Well, Maryland Cup had been a very profitable company with a highly family oriented kind of culture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Maryland Cup曾经是一家非常赚钱的公司，有着高度以家庭为导向的文化。

sentences.en: You know, the bosses would dress up as Santa Claus, you know, turkeys to all everybody at Thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 你知道，老板们会打扮成圣诞老人，感恩节时给每个人发火鸡。

sentences.en: You know, that kind of like paternalistic, we are all one big family company thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种家长式的“我们都是一家人”的公司氛围。

sentences.en: Once they go into Fort Howard, it becomes a true just kind of like we're going to have to make money.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们被Fort Howard收购，就变成了一种纯粹的“我们必须赚钱”的模式。

sentences.en: So all these people get laid off.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些人都被解雇了。

sentences.en: They cut pensions.
sentences.zh: 他们削减了养老金。

sentences.en: They do all this stuff that's basically like the plot of Tommy Boy, kind of.
sentences.zh: 他们做的所有这些事情，基本上就像电影《Tommy Boy》的情节一样。

sentences.en: You remember this movie with Chris Farley about Sandusky, Ohio?
sentences.zh: 你还记得那部Chris Farley主演的关于俄亥俄州桑达斯基的电影吗？

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, we're in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，我们有大麻烦了。

sentences.en: Zelensky Industries has an offer on the table to buy us out.
sentences.zh: Zelensky Industries出价要收购我们。

sentences.en: But as you realize, Callahan has been family owned since Tommy's great grandfather laid the first brick.
sentences.zh: 但你们也知道，自从Tommy的曾祖父铺下第一块砖以来，Callahan一直都是家族企业。

sentences.en: And I'll be damned if that's going to change on my watch.
sentences.zh: 如果在我任内发生这种事，我绝不答应。

sentences.en: Frankie, if we sell while our value is still high, everyone won't stop.
sentences.zh: Frankie，如果我们趁价值还高的时候卖掉，大家就不会失业了。

sentences.en: You know, but it's played out many, many, many, many times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但这出戏已经上演过无数次了。

sentences.en: And in the end,
sentences.zh: 最后，

sentences.en: what ends up happening is that Fort Howard itself then is bought by a private equity firm who then goes and combines a bunch of the different paper cup and disposable goods companies into one kind of larger entity and then spins it out loaded with a bunch of debt.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是，Fort Howard自己被一家私募股权公司收购，然后他们把一堆不同的纸杯和一次性用品公司合并成一个更大的实体，接着背负着巨额债务将其拆分上市。

sentences.en: And this is kind of a classic move that happens in private equity because you can borrow against these companies, pay your investors,
sentences.zh: 这是私募股权中典型的操作，因为你可以利用这些公司进行抵押借贷，支付给投资者，

sentences.en: and then spin out this other company that then is like sort of floating in the ocean like with rocks tied around its feet, right?
sentences.zh: 然后把这家公司抛出去，就像脚上绑着石头漂在海里一样，对吧？

sentences.en: So, operationally, like from making cups and straws and all this stuff, they're still making money.
sentences.zh: 所以，在运营层面，比如制造杯子和吸管这些东西，他们仍然在赚钱。

sentences.en: But because they have to pay all this debt, they're like deeply in the red.
sentences.zh: 但因为他们必须偿还所有这些债务，他们陷入了严重的亏损。

sentences.en: So, then they have to lay off people.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不得不裁员。

sentences.en: Then they have to close factories.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不关闭工厂。

sentences.en: And it is just the classic story of kind of like vulture capitalism.
sentences.zh: 这就是典型的“秃鹫资本主义”故事。

sentences.en: And the fact that the straw, like the stupid straw, this like empty vessel somehow also is tied up in the financialization of America just says one thing to me,
sentences.zh: 事实上，吸管，这种愚蠢的吸管，这种空心的容器，竟然也与美国的金融化纠缠在一起，这对我来说只说明了一件事，

sentences.en: which is that every single goddamn thing is tied up with this kind of system of production.
sentences.zh: 那就是每一件该死的事情都与这种生产体系捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: Can banning straws really make a dent in our ecological problems?
sentences.zh: 禁止吸管真的能缓解我们的生态问题吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's just not up to the scale of the problem.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，这根本解决不了问题的规模。

sentences.en: You know, I think the through line I see with all this stuff, because obviously it's hard to connect, you know, an 1888 patent to the, you know, first artificial straw to,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为我从所有这些事情中看到的脉络，因为显然很难将1888年的专利，也就是第一根人造吸管，与，你知道，

sentences.en: you know, financial capitalism in its current form.
sentences.zh: 当前形式的金融资本主义联系起来。

sentences.en: Here's the through line as I see it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所看到的脉络。

sentences.en: The country has shed manufacturing jobs for decades.
sentences.zh: 这个国家几十年来一直在流失制造业工作岗位。

sentences.en: Straws contribute.
sentences.zh: 吸管也有份。

sentences.en: They're a little tiny share to environmental disasters that are far beyond it.
sentences.zh: 它们对远超其影响范围的环境灾难贡献了一点点微小的份额。

sentences.en: I mean, the economy continues to work in this way that concentrates wealth, you know, for the very richest people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，经济继续以这种方式运作，为最富有的人集中财富，你知道。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: the sodas that are even like passing through the straws into people's stomachs are contributing to this obesity epidemic that threatens to actually roll back the public health reforMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些通过吸管进入人们胃里的苏打水，也在加剧肥胖流行病，这实际上威胁到要扭转公共卫生改革的成果，

sentences.en: That actually got people's life expectancies to grow in previous eras.
sentences.zh: 而这些改革在过去确实提高了人们的预期寿命。

sentences.en: And there's just this vast system now that's attached to the straw that helped really to create, you know, disposable products and then disposable companies.
sentences.zh: 现在有一个庞大的系统附着在吸管上，它确实帮助创造了，你知道，一次性产品，然后是一次性公司。

sentences.en: And finally kind of disposable people, both the workers who work within this system,
sentences.zh: 最后是某种一次性的人，既包括在这个系统中工作的工人，

sentences.en: but also people who just have to live with all of these crises that have been created by structures far beyond their control.
sentences.zh: 也包括那些不得不忍受所有这些由他们无法控制的结构所造成的危机的人们。

sentences.en: And so it was almost like, though we can all see that going on around us.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎就像，尽管我们都能看到周围发生的一切。

sentences.en: It's kind of only when you focus down on like the most tiny thing that you can see that massive structure in this kind of very pure way.
sentences.zh: 只有当你聚焦于最微小的事物时，你才能以这种非常纯粹的方式看到那个巨大的结构。

sentences.en: Arguably the most significant technological achievement of the 20th century, at least according to one of the descendants of the inventor.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是20世纪最伟大的技术成就，至少发明者的后代之一是这么认为的。

sentences.en: It's the story of the bendy straw after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来是弯曲吸管的故事。

sentences.en: As Alexis mentioned earlier, the Maryland Cup Corporation got bought out and then its buyers got bought out and so on up the capitalist fast food chain.
sentences.zh: 正如Alexis之前提到的，Maryland Cup公司被收购，然后它的买家又被收购，以此类推，沿着资本主义快餐连锁的链条向上。

sentences.en: But before Maryland Cup sold their family business, they grew in part by acquiring a revolutionary key patent from another company.
sentences.zh: 但在Maryland Cup卖掉家族企业之前，他们通过从另一家公司获得一项革命性的关键专利而实现了部分增长。

sentences.en: Kurt Colstead is here to talk about that other family owned business that they bought out, the Flexible Straw Corporation.
sentences.zh: Kurt Colstead在这里谈谈他们收购的另一家家族企业，Flexible Straw Corporation。

sentences.en: So first, a bit of context.
sentences.zh: 首先，介绍一点背景。

sentences.en: As Alexis pointed out, we'll never really know when humans first started using straws.
sentences.zh: 正如Alexis指出的，我们永远无法真正知道人类是什么时候开始使用吸管的。

sentences.en: But there's this Sumerian tomb that dates back about 5,000 years.
sentences.zh: 但有一个苏美尔人的坟墓，可以追溯到大约5000年前。

sentences.en: And on its seal, there are these figures who appear to be drinking from straws.
sentences.zh: 在它的印章上，有这些看起来像是在用吸管喝水的人物。

sentences.en: Sure enough, when people opened up the tomb, they found this ornate drinking tube inside.
sentences.zh: 果然，当人们打开坟墓时，在里面发现了这种华丽的饮水管。

sentences.en: It's made of gold and decked out with these precious stones.
sentences.zh: 它由黄金制成，装饰着这些珍贵的宝石。

sentences.en: It's really fancy and it's really old.
sentences.zh: 它非常精致，而且非常古老。

sentences.en: And it's probably not the oldest straw that ever existed.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能不是有史以来最古老的吸管。

sentences.en: It's just the oldest one we've found.
sentences.zh: 它只是我们发现的最古老的一根。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It may not even be close.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能差得远呢。

sentences.en: But setting its expensive materials aside, it's still just a straight tube.
sentences.zh: 但撇开它昂贵的材料不谈，它仍然只是一根直管。

sentences.en: A bit more durable, a bit more precious, sure.
sentences.zh: 当然，更耐用一点，更珍贵一点。

sentences.en: But otherwise, not that different from a modern grass or paper or plastic straw.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，与现代的草制、纸制或塑料吸管并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: So in a lot of ways, straw design hasn't fundamentally changed for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 所以在很多方面，吸管的设计几千年来并没有发生根本性的改变。

sentences.en: Or at least it didn't until the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 或者至少在20世纪30年代之前是这样。

sentences.en: And that's when the Flexible Straw came into existence.
sentences.zh: 那时，可弯曲吸管诞生了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as the story goes, the inventor, Joseph B.
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，发明家Joseph B. Friedman带他的女儿去旧金山的一家甜品店喝奶昔，那家店是他兄弟开的。

sentences.en: Friedman, took his daughter to get a milkshake in San Francisco at a sweet shop owned by his brother.
sentences.zh: 但当他看着女儿费力地使用这种普通的直吸管时，他心想，

sentences.en: But as he's watching his daughter struggle with this normal straight straw, he thinks to himself,
sentences.zh: 嘿，你知道，也许有更好的方法来做这件事。

sentences.en: hey, you know, maybe there's a better way to do this.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这就是典型的，你发现了一个问题，然后解决了一个问题。

sentences.en: And that's like the classic, you see a problem, you fix a problem.
sentences.zh: 但这家伙并不是专业做吸管的。

sentences.en: But this guy wasn't a straw maker by trade.
sentences.zh: 他是如何创造出这个新物体的？

sentences.en: How did he create this new object?
sentences.zh: 所以他从这种简单的现有纸吸管开始。

sentences.en: So he starts out with this simple existing paper straw.
sentences.zh: 然后他在颈部插入了一颗金属螺丝。

sentences.en: And then he slots in a metal screw into the neck.
sentences.zh: 然后他把牙线缠绕在螺丝上，这样当他拧紧时，就会产生褶皱。

sentences.en: And then he wraps dental floss around the screw so that when he tightens it down, it creates ridges.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这些褶皱让它能够弯曲，你知道，就像手风琴一样。

sentences.en: And these ridges allow the thing to bend, you know, like an accordion.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要利用螺丝的螺纹来提供凹槽，然后拧紧它，再把它取出来。

sentences.en: So you just use the screws threading to provide the groove and then you tighten it and take it back out again.
sentences.zh: 再把它取出来。

sentences.en: Take it back out again.
sentences.zh: 你就得到了一根可弯曲吸管。

sentences.en: And you have a FlexiStraw.
sentences.zh: 然后你就得到了一根可弯曲吸管。

sentences.en: And then you get a FlexiStraw.
sentences.zh: 所以真的任何人都能做到这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: So like really anybody could have done this, right?
sentences.zh: 他在专利申请中也说得很清楚。

sentences.en: And he's really clear about this too in the patent application.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，我没有发明手风琴。

sentences.en: He's like, look, I didn't invent the accordion.
sentences.zh: 我没有发明吸管。

sentences.en: I didn't invent the straw.
sentences.zh: 我所做的只是把这种灵活性的想法与这种，你知道，用于饮用的直管结合起来。

sentences.en: All I did was I combined this idea of flexibility with this, you know, straight tube for drinking out of.
sentences.zh: 所以他用这种“百战天龙”式的方法把它创造了出来。

sentences.en: So he MacGyver's this thing into existence.
sentences.zh: 它是否立即彻底改变了整个行业？

sentences.en: And does it revolutionize the industry right away?
sentences.zh: 它有什么作用？

sentences.en: What does it do?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些可弯曲吸管花了一段时间才流行起来，这有点令人震惊。

sentences.en: It actually took a while for these FlexiStraws to catch on, which is kind of shocking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他兄弟开了一家苏打水店。

sentences.en: Well, because his brother owned a soda shop.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他有进入市场的渠道。

sentences.en: Like he's got a path to market.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 然而不知何故，他花了大约10年时间才开始销售这些东西。

sentences.en: And yet somehow it takes him like 10 years to start selling these things.
sentences.zh: 靠希望生活的时间太长了。

sentences.en: That's a long time to live on hope.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 他最终不得不兼职做其他工作。

sentences.en: And he ended up taking other jobs on the side.
sentences.zh: 他做过房地产经纪人，勉强维持生计。

sentences.en: He did some work as a real estate agent, sort of keep it alive.
sentences.zh: 他还从投资该业务的兄弟那里获得了资金注入，

sentences.en: And he also got cash infusions from his brothers who invested in the business,
sentences.zh: 并从他的妹妹Betty那里得到了商业帮助，据许多人说，她才是这个业务的幕后大脑。

sentences.en: got some business help from his sister, Betty, who by many accounts is sort of the brains of the operation.
sentences.zh: 最后，10年后，他们有了第一批买家，但这与孩子或苏打水店毫无关系。

sentences.en: And then finally, 10 years later, they get their first buyers and it has nothing to do with kids or soda shops.
sentences.zh: 那么，第一批购买可弯曲吸管的人是谁？

sentences.en: So who are the first people to buy FlexiStraws?
sentences.zh: 第一批购买可弯曲吸管的人是谁？

sentences.en: It ends up being these large hospitals, which if you think about it, makes perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 最终这些吸管被用在了大型医院里，如果你仔细想想，这完全合情合理。

sentences.en: They've got injured patients, disabled patients, people lying in beds who have trouble sitting up.
sentences.zh: 医院里有受伤的病人、残障人士，还有躺在床上连坐起来都很困难的人。

sentences.en: And so these FlexiStraws, which are, you know, bendable, disposable, sanitary, they're just perfect for these hospital environments.
sentences.zh: 所以这种可弯曲、一次性且卫生的FlexiStraw吸管，简直是医院环境的完美选择。

sentences.en: And from there, of course, they go on to restaurants and kids' juice boxes and all that.
sentences.zh: 当然，从那里开始，它们逐渐进入了餐厅、儿童果汁盒等各种场景。

sentences.en: But they start out in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 但它们最初确实是在医院里开始使用的。

sentences.en: It's a really interesting example of universal design where it's really taken by a community that needs it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于通用设计的非常有趣的例子，它最初被有需要的群体所采用。

sentences.en: And then everyone realizes, hey, these are kind of nice for us, too.
sentences.zh: 然后大家意识到，嘿，这对我们来说其实也挺好用的。

sentences.en: You know, as we mentioned before, there's some movement to have all plastic straws banned.
sentences.zh: 如前所述，现在有一些呼声要求全面禁用塑料吸管。

sentences.en: Do they still have a place in society?
sentences.zh: 它们在社会中还有一席之地吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's really debatable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实很有争议。

sentences.en: And it's still being debated.
sentences.zh: 而且目前争论仍在继续。

sentences.en: And some people are saying, hey, look, let's go back to these paper bendy straws.
sentences.zh: 有些人说，嘿，看，我们还是回到那种纸质的可弯曲吸管吧。

sentences.en: That worked, right?
sentences.zh: 那种不是挺好用的吗？

sentences.en: That's what Friedman was inventing with in the first place.
sentences.zh: 那正是弗里德曼最初发明的东西。

sentences.en: But then a lot of disability rights activists are saying, hey, you know, that's great for some people, but they can also fall apart.
sentences.zh: 但很多残疾人权利活动家表示，嘿，这对某些人来说确实不错，但它们也容易散架。

sentences.en: They're not that durable.
sentences.zh: 它们不够耐用。

sentences.en: And there's also an argument that, OK, well, then we should use reusable ones, right, that are sort of more eco-friendly, like glass or metal.
sentences.zh: 还有一种观点认为，好吧，那我们应该使用可重复使用的吸管，比如玻璃或金属材质的，那样更环保，对吧？

sentences.en: But those are hard to keep clean.
sentences.zh: 但那些很难保持清洁。

sentences.en: They can break.
sentences.zh: 而且它们可能会碎。

sentences.en: So there are issues with all these different types.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些不同类型的吸管都存在各自的问题。

sentences.en: And for a certain demographic of people who really needs them, there's a strong argument for keeping around plastic bendy straws.
sentences.zh: 对于某些真正需要它们的人群来说，保留塑料可弯曲吸管有着充分的理由。

sentences.en: You can see pictures and patents of Friedman's original Flex Straw and old vintage print ads for them, too.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站上看到弗里德曼最初的Flex Straw的照片和专利，还有当年的老式印刷广告。

sentences.en: They're delightful.
sentences.zh: 它们非常有趣。

sentences.en: That's on our website.
sentences.zh: 这些都在我们的网站上。

sentences.en: It's at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 网址是99pi.org。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by senior editor Delaney Hall, based on the story Disposable America by Alexis Madrigal, written for The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由高级编辑Delaney Hall制作，故事基于Alexis Madrigal为《大西洋月刊》撰写的《一次性美国》一文。

sentences.en: Mix and tech production by Sharif Youssef.
sentences.zh: 混音和技术制作由Sharif Youssef负责。

sentences.en: Music by Sean Rial.
sentences.zh: 音乐由Sean Rial创作。

sentences.en: Katie Mingle is our senior producer.
sentences.zh: Katie Mingle是我们的高级制作人。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: Kurt Kolstad是数字总监。

sentences.en: The rest of the team is Vivian Lee, Avery Truffelman, Joe Rosenberg, Emmett Fitzgerald, Taryn Mazza, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 团队其他成员包括Vivian Lee、Avery Truffelman、Joe Rosenberg、Emmett Fitzgerald、Taryn Mazza，以及我，Roman Mars。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW电台的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心美丽的Radio Row制作。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is a member of Radiotopia from PRX, a fiercely independent collective of the most innovative shows in all of podcasting.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》是PRX旗下Radiotopia的成员，这是一个由播客界最具创新性的节目组成的独立联盟。

sentences.en: Find them all at radiotopia.fm.
sentences.zh: 你可以在radiotopia.fm找到所有节目。

sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上关注我@RomanMars，或者关注节目@99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram、Tumblr和Reddit上。

sentences.en: But you can listen to and read a ton more stories that use everyday objects to tell the story of the whole world at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在99pi.org收听并阅读更多关于如何通过日常物品讲述世界故事的内容。
